title: Banks Create Money Out of Thin Air. Here's Proof #shorts
description:
Your bank doesn't lend out your savings. When it makes a loan, it creates a brand-new deposit: new money. The Bank of England said it plainly in 2014: banks create money by making loans.

- In the UK, about 97% of money was bank deposits, not cash (Bank of England, 2014)
- In the US, only about 1 in 10 dollars is physical cash: $2.48 trillion of currency vs a $23.4 trillion M2 money supply (FRED)
- The US reserve requirement has been 0% since March 26, 2020 (Federal Reserve)
- Paying off a loan destroys that money again

Watch next: The Fed Just Raised Rates https://youtu.be/JlrNu4toOc8

Sources: Bank of England, "Money creation in the modern economy", Quarterly Bulletin 2014 Q1; Federal Reserve Board (reserve requirements, March 2020); FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis: WCURCIR (Oct 28, 2026), M2SL (Sep 2026).
